skill.name: env-manager
skill.description: Manage environment variable documentation, validation patterns, and safe configuration examples for application projects.
skill.summary: Guides teams through environment variable validation, documentation, and safer secret handling.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives caused by Markdown examples, placeholder configuration values, and environment-management documentation. I found no executable code, unauthorized network behavior, credential exfiltration intent, or prompt injection in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Placeholder secrets resemble real credential patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Keep using obvious placeholders and add comments that users must never paste real secrets into prompts or examples.

remediation.issue: Many examples appear inside executable-looking code blocks.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples clearly as documentation snippets so automated scanners and users understand they are not skill runtime code.

static_findings.snippet: throw new Error('API_KEY environment variable is required');
- Never commit actual `.env` files with secrets

content.value_statement: Environment variables are easy to miss, duplicate, or expose. This skill helps document, validate, and harden configuration across environments.
actual_capabilities: Identifies environment variables that code expects or documents.
Builds .env.example style templates with required and optional values.
Explains validation patterns for Node.js and Python projects.
Documents common secret names, service prefixes, defaults, and formats.
Provides safer handling guidance for .env files and production secrets.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples; it does not execute validation by itself.
It cannot verify real deployment settings unless project files are available.
It should not receive live secret values in prompts or examples.
Generated templates still require human review before production use.

use_cases.title: Prepare a New Service Configuration
use_cases.description: Create a clear starting template for required database, cache, auth, and service settings.

use_cases.title: Audit Environment Drift
use_cases.description: Compare documented variables with application usage before staging or production release.

use_cases.title: Improve Secret Handling Documentation
use_cases.description: Document which values are sensitive and where production secrets should be stored.

prompt_templates.title: List Required Variables
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project and list required environment variables with short descriptions and safe example values.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Example Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a .env.example template for this app. Use placeholders only, group values by service, and mark optional variables.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Configuration Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Check these environment variables for missing validation, weak defaults, and unsafe production settings. Summarize fixes by priority.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Environment Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a development, staging, and production environment policy. Include naming rules, secret storage, rotation guidance, and documentation standards.

output_examples.input: Document the required variables for a Node.js API with Postgres, Redis, and JWT authentication.
output_examples.output: A grouped variable reference with required status, safe placeholder examples, validation notes, and secret handling warnings.

output_examples.input: Review our current configuration before production release.
output: Flags missing validation for authentication secrets.
Recommends moving cloud credentials to a managed secret store.
Highlights development-only values that should not reach production.

output_examples.input: Create onboarding notes for local environment setup.
output_examples.output: A short setup guide that copies the example template, explains local overrides, and warns against committing private values.

best_practices: Use placeholders in examples and never include live secrets.
Validate required variables at application startup.
Store production secrets in a managed secret service.
anti_patterns: Do not commit real .env files or private key files.
Do not use production credentials in local examples.
Do not rely on silent defaults for security-critical settings.

faq.question: Does this skill read my real environment variables?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance from project files or text that you share.

faq.question: Can it generate a safe .env.example file?
faq.answer: Yes. It can produce templates with placeholders, comments, and required or optional labels.

faq.question: Should I paste secrets into prompts?
faq.answer: No. Replace secrets with placeholders before using the skill.

faq.question: Does it support both Node.js and Python projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes examples for common validation patterns in both ecosystems.

faq.question: Can it replace a secret manager?
faq.answer: No. It documents and recommends secret management practices, but it does not store secrets.

faq.question: Why does it mention AWS, Stripe, and SendGrid?
faq.answer: They are example services used to show common naming and documentation patterns.
